categories.label: Financial
questions: What is the exact contracting entity and which audited statements cover it rather than only its parent group?
What do the latest available cash flow, liquidity, debt maturity and profitability disclosures show, and what periods do they cover?
Are there insolvency proceedings, going-concern warnings, covenant breaches, restatements or rating changes?
Would customer concentration, refinancing needs or project losses affect the proposed order?
Which current financial facts remain unavailable and must be requested from the supplier?
source_types: Audited annual and interim financial statements
Official securities filings and exchange announcements
Official insolvency and corporate registers
Rating agency's own dated rating publication
Supplier financial documents supplied by the buyer
red_flags: Entity-specific insolvency or going-concern disclosure
Negative operating cash flow with near-term debt pressure
Material restatement or covenant breach
Current financial statements unavailable for the contracting entity
follow_ups: Request recent entity-level accounts, liquidity forecast and debt maturity schedule
Verify warning status and later corrective disclosures
Ask finance to review payment terms, guarantees and order exposure

categories.label: Legal & governance
questions: What are the registered name, jurisdiction, registration identifier and ownership links of the contracting entity?
Are there relevant sanctions, export restrictions, debarments or ownership/control concerns in the transaction's jurisdictions?
Do official records establish material litigation, regulatory investigations, penalties or corruption findings?
Is each matter an allegation, pending proceeding, final decision, appeal or resolved case?
Which governance controls and corrective actions are described, and what evidence supports their implementation?
source_types: Official corporate and beneficial ownership registers where accessible
Official sanctions lists and underlying legal acts
Court dockets, judgments and regulator decisions
Official procurement exclusion registers
Company governance and compliance disclosures
red_flags: Potential identity-matched sanctions or debarment record requiring expert review
Material unresolved regulatory or court finding
Opaque contracting identity or unexplained ownership discrepancy
Unsupported claim that a legal matter has been resolved
follow_ups: Resolve name matches using registration identifiers and ownership evidence
Obtain current official case status and supplier response
Route jurisdiction and transaction-specific restrictions to the responsible compliance reviewer

categories.label: Country exposure
questions: Where are the relevant production sites, critical sub-tier sources and logistics routes, distinct from headquarters?
Which current conflict, political instability, trade restriction or border disruption affects those locations?
What flood, earthquake, extreme-weather, energy or infrastructure exposure affects the relevant site?
What location-specific continuity arrangements and alternative routes are evidenced?
Which locations or exposure links remain unknown, and what country indicators are only contextual?
source_types: Supplier facility and sourcing disclosures
Government trade, customs and export-control notices
Official emergency, geological and meteorological agencies
World Bank governance indicators with edition and uncertainty
Official transport and infrastructure disruption notices
red_flags: Confirmed facility or route exposure to an active disruption
Single-region concentration without evidenced alternatives
Restrictions plausibly affecting the specific product or transaction
Country conclusion inferred solely from headquarters or nationality
follow_ups: Request facility and sub-tier location map for the proposed component
Check latest official disruption and restriction notices
Verify alternate sites, logistics routes and recovery assumptions

categories.label: People & safety
questions: What site-specific evidence exists for serious injuries, fatalities, safety enforcement and corrective actions?
Are there credible forced-labour, child-labour, discrimination, working-time or freedom-of-association concerns?
Are strikes, industrial disputes or workforce shortages affecting relevant operations?
Do worker grievance channels and safety management processes have evidence of implementation?
What is the reporting period, workforce scope and definition behind any incident rate?
source_types: Labour and occupational safety regulator records
Official court and enforcement decisions
Company sustainability and site safety disclosures
Worker or trade union original statements
Independent audit records with scope, date and issuer
red_flags: Serious incident with unresolved corrective actions
Official forced-labour finding or substantiated worker-rights concern
Ongoing dispute affecting the relevant site
Group-wide safety claims used to imply a specific site has been audited
follow_ups: Request site-specific incident history and corrective-action closure evidence
Seek original worker, regulator and supplier accounts
Verify audit date, scope and remediation rather than treating a policy as proof

categories.label: Operations
questions: Can the actual site manufacture the required component at the required quality, capacity and lead time?
What recalls, quality failures, production interruptions or delivery problems are evidenced?
Where are single-source dependencies and critical sub-tier visibility gaps?
What cyber incidents, operational technology dependencies and continuity or recovery arrangements are evidenced?
Which certificates, rail-specific approvals and customer performance data apply to this component and site?
source_types: Official product recall and safety notices
Supplier production and continuity disclosures
Certificate issuer or official certification registers
Official cyber incident disclosures and regulator notices
Buyer delivery, quality and capacity records
Component and site-specific technical documentation
red_flags: Unresolved recall or quality escape affecting proposed parts
Critical single-source dependency without a verified recovery option
Cyber disruption with unresolved production impact
Missing or expired component/site-specific qualification evidence
follow_ups: Request capacity, lead-time and recent delivery/quality evidence
Verify certificate issuer, expiry and product/site scope
Request recovery test results, sub-tier map and alternate-source plan

categories.label: Reputation
questions: Which recent credible adverse reports concern the correct entity, sites or products?
What original event, court record or regulator document supports each report?
Are multiple articles independent sources or repetitions of one original claim?
What supplier response, later correction, resolution or contradictory evidence exists?
What customer, market or public-trust consequence is evidenced rather than inferred from negative wording?
source_types: Original regulator, court and company statements behind news
Independent original reporting with named evidence
Company responses and published corrections
Original customer or worker statements
Dated company market disclosures
red_flags: Repeated independently evidenced material misconduct or unresolved controversy
Substantial contradiction between public assurances and original records
Unresolved credible allegation relevant to the sourcing decision
Many syndicated headlines incorrectly counted as independent corroboration
follow_ups: Trace reporting to the original event and entity
Seek later case status, correction and supplier response
Assess demonstrated procurement relevance with the buyer
